correctness.rationale: For \(0<\lambda<1\) the anchor's scalar objective is strictly convex, so Jensen equality holds exactly when every \(r_j=1\). The HJW probability identity then forces equal column moduli in both rows, and row orthogonality is precisely the zero complex barycenter of the relative phases. The converse reconstructs an admissible co-isometry. Rank two and the two-vector zero-sum equation give the exact support-two minimum and antipodal equal weights. Phase independence is independently verified from the one-qubit determinant formula.
risks: No claim is made at \(\lambda=0\) or \(\lambda=1\), where strict convexity and rank-two hypotheses degenerate.
Finite checker output is corroboration only; the infinite statement is proved analytically.
